title: The Laundromat Math: How Boring Businesses Really Make Money
description:
A laundromat looks boring, but the math behind it teaches almost everything about small business: revenue, the lease, equipment, owner earnings, valuation and how buyers really pay. Here's the full breakdown with a simple example.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:45 How we got the numbers
2:15 Angle 1: The numbers
4:08 Lesson 1. Demand comes first
5:14 Lesson 2. Revenue has layers
6:13 Lesson 3. Rent is the silent partner
7:12 Lesson 4. Utilities move with volume
8:16 Lesson 5. Equipment wears out
9:21 Lesson 6. Labor is a choice
10:39 Lesson 7. Value is a multiple
11:55 Lesson 8. Most buyers use debt
13:16 Lesson 9. Leverage cuts both ways
14:17 Lesson 10. Compare to the boring alternative
15:22 Lesson 11. Records tell the truth
16:23 Lesson 12. Improve, then sell or hold
17:25 The same math, everywhere
19:11 Three owners, three outcomes
21:11 Five ways to raise profit without raising risk
22:30 The exit: what happens when you sell
23:34 Ten red flags when buying a small business
26:31 Angle 2: The psychology
28:07 Angle 3: The playbook
29:35 Questions people ask
32:37 Recap: the laundromat math
33:33 What to do next

Sources:
- Example laundromat figures: simplified illustration built for teaching, not an industry average or a real business
- U.S. Small Business Administration, 7(a) loan program (guaranteed loans, including for business acquisitions; equity injection requirements)
- Bureau of Labor Statistics, Business Employment Dynamics (business survival rates)
- Loan payment example: $270,000 over 10 years at an illustrative 10.5% interest rate
- Market comparison: stated illustrative 7% average yearly return

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video13.md

This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Numbers are illustrations, not promises.
